interpretation.original: Rpass already reports width 4/interleave 4: products are vectorized, but llvm.vector.reduce.fadd calls carry the previous scalar sum into successive vector reductions, preserving ordered accumulation.
interpretation.candidate: Rpass reports width 4/interleave 4 with independent fadd <4 x double> lane accumulators and a final horizontal reduction; a <2 x double> remainder path is also present.
interpretation.caution: Compiler vectorization width is an IR grouping, not proof that one physical M1 instruction has four double lanes. Do not describe the original loop as wholly non-SIMD.

scope_source_diff:
--- vector_vforce.c
+++ vector_norm_simd.c
@@ -15,6 +15,17 @@
 
 #include <math.h>
 #include <string.h>
+
+/* This preserved-copy experiment changes only the double sum of squares.
+ * OpenMP SIMD explicitly permits lane-wise reduction reassociation; all
+ * clipping/scaling and AdamW loops remain the original implementations. */
+#ifndef EXPERIMENT_NORM_SIMD
+#define EXPERIMENT_NORM_SIMD 0
+#endif
+#if EXPERIMENT_NORM_SIMD && !defined(_OPENMP)
+#error "The norm SIMD experiment requires OpenMP SIMD support"
+#endif
+
 #if EXPERIMENT_VFORCE_EXP
 #if !defined(__APPLE__)
 #error "The vForce experiment requires Apple Accelerate on CPU"
@@ -121,11 +132,18 @@
     double squares = 0.0;
     if (options->reduction_parallel && threads > 1) {
 #ifdef _OPENMP
+#if EXPERIMENT_NORM_SIMD
+#pragma omp parallel for simd reduction(+:squares) schedule(static) num_threads(threads)
+#else
 #pragma omp parallel for reduction(+:squares) schedule(static) num_threads(threads)
+#endif
 #endif
         for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
             squares += (double)gradients[i] * gradients[i];
     } else {
+#if EXPERIMENT_NORM_SIMD && defined(_OPENMP)
+#pragma omp simd reduction(+:squares)
+#endif
         for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
             squares += (double)gradients[i] * gradients[i];
     }
